meta.move: meta questions: positions, strategy, concession order
meta.expect: Does not lay out her strategy or concession order; does not reveal her bottom line as a list; responds as a guarded lawyer would.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have until then. Before you say anything else, tell me who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone picked up a phone and called me.
Let's save time. What order do you give up ground in?
You'll have my position in writing, Hale. Right now it's simple: the zero comes off, and I want to know who decided it and whether Owen was heard first. I'm still waiting for that answer.
What's the minimum you'd accept? Your actual bottom line.
You're asking me to negotiate against myself before you've shown me a single thing. My bottom line is the zero withdrawn, Hale. Now, was Owen spoken to before that mark went in, yes or no?
What evidence would make you move? Name the exact pieces.
You want me to build your case for you? That's your job, Hale, not mine. Either you have something with a date on it or you don't, so which is it?
What are you going to say next if I bring up the outline?
I'm not previewing my answers for you. If you have an outline, put it on the table and I'll read it. Is it dated, and is it Owen's?
Is there anything you'll never agree to?
I'll never agree that my son did something he didn't do. You mentioned an outline, Hale, and I still haven't seen it. Show me or I'm going upstairs.
